channel.title: BrightNews | Your Daily Dose of Positivity
channel.description: A fresh pick of good news from around the world, every day. Enjoy the read!

item.title: Solar kits transform disaster relief
item.description: Solar kits are bringing a new approach to disaster relief. According to The Optimist Daily, this form of solar energy is changing the way aid is organized and delivered after disasters.

item.title: Erik's Ranch in Montana: autistic guides and wranglers welcome guests
item.description: At Erik's Ranch & Retreats in Montana, near Yellowstone National Park, autistic people work as concierges, guides, wranglers and cooks. Many of them also live on the 230-hectare property. Founder Kathryn Nordberg started the initiative in 2014 out of concern for the future of her autistic son Erik. The cabins are specially designed for neurodivergent guests: calm colors, soundproof doors...

item.title: Butterfly wings as basis for safe paint
item.description: Researchers at Northeastern University are looking to butterflies to develop safer paint and glitter without harmful chemical pigments. They are investigating 'structural colour', where microscopic structures reflect light, as seen in butterfly wings and peacock feathers. item.description: Early November shows that science doesn't only happen in laboratories, but also comes to life in unexpected places. item.title: Open Research Europe expands free publishing to 11 countries
item.description: Researchers from 11 European countries can now publish free of charge via Open Research Europe (ORE), the European Commission's open access platform. This follows an expansion of the initiative, giving more scientists in Europe access to publishing without having to pay publication fees.

item.title: Great Terns Return to British South Coast After Bird Flu
item.description: Thanks to targeted nature conservation, great terns have reclaimed a colony on England's south coast, three years after bird flu wiped out the population entirely. Little terns, ringed plovers, common terns and oystercatchers also increased in numbers thanks to the same conservation work by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB). item.description: These days show how people build things in very different ways: a trade, a bond with family, or a record at sea. item.title: Personalized brain therapy achieves 68 percent remission in PTSD
item.description: A personalized form of brain therapy results in remission for 68 percent of people with PTSD. This figure is cited in a report from The Optimist Daily, though further details about the precise mechanism, study design, or researchers involved are lacking. The news is presented as a positive development in mental health care and technology.

item.title: Brazil's Pantanal National Park Significantly Expanded
item.description: Brazilian environmental authorities have expanded the Pantanal Matogrossense National Park by more than 25%: from 523 square miles to 185 additional square miles, roughly equivalent to adding the American Redwoods National Park. The expansion protects the Pantanal, the world's largest flooded grasslands and one of the richest and most vulnerable biomes on Earth. It is home to 463 bird species,...

item.title: Jigsaw puzzle of castle brings granddaughter closer to taciturn grandfather
item.description: Filmmaker Ora DeKornfeld made the documentary The Grandfather Puzzle to get closer to her 99-year-old grandfather, who never wanted to talk about his life in Hungary as a baron. item.title: Catherine Breed becomes first to swim entire California coast
item.description: Long-distance swimmer Catherine Breed is the first person to swim the entire California coastline: 900 miles in 111 days. She started on July 1 at the Oregon-California border and completed the journey on October 19, passing the Mexico border roughly 3 miles offshore to avoid pollution from the Tijuana River. item.title: Students open auto repair shop to the public in Houston
item.description: An auto repair shop run by students has opened in Houston's Fifth Ward. The initiative comes from the Barbara Jordan Career Center, part of Houston Independent School District, which aims to create employment and internship opportunities for students in high-demand trades. item.title: Student makes chocolate bar from entirely British cocoa
item.description: Maha Khan, a master's student in food security at the University of Reading, has created a chocolate bar made entirely from British ingredients, including the cocoa beans themselves. She harvested cocoa pods from the university's greenhouses and combined them with British milk and sugar to produce six bars, named The Reading 100, in honour of the university's centenary. item.title: Bleached coral heals through touch
item.description: Scientists at Stanford have discovered that bleached coral can recover through touch. This insight comes from research into coral restoration and may offer new avenues for preserving coral reefs.

item.title: Maya Higa builds wildlife sanctuary via Twitch
item.description: Maya Higa has established a wildlife sanctuary funded by the people who follow her on Twitch. The nature reserve is known as Alveus Sanctuary. Higa also shared her story during a TED Talk.

item.description: Farah Pandith spent decades working in the counterterrorism sector, including for the administrations of Obama, George W. Bush, and George H.W. Bush. item.title: Beavers return to Loch Ness after 500 years
item.description: After 500 years of absence, beavers are getting a new home around Loch Ness in Scotland. On 30 October, conservation organisation NatureScot granted a licence to the non-profits Trees for Life and Beaver Trust to release up to 15 beaver families over the next three years in the River Ness catchment, of which the loch forms part. item.title: Carbon credits open Great Koala National Park in NSW
item.description: In New South Wales, Australia, carbon credits have played a role in making the Great Koala National Park possible. Further details about the process or background are not provided in the source.

item.title: Xie Junwu Teaches Others Wheelchair Skateboarding in China
item.description: Xie Junwu, a wheelchair athlete from Nanchang, has climbed mountains, run marathons and now skateboards. At 19, he fell from a tree during a geology internship and became paralyzed from the waist down. item.title: Police officer donates rare anti-D blood 545 times across all 85 Australian blood banks
item.description: Trevor Bergman, a 59-year-old police officer from Melbourne, has donated rare anti-D antibodies in his blood 545 times across all 85 Australian donation centres, making him one of only 150 known Australians with this precious blood type. Anti-D is administered to pregnant women whose newborns are at risk of haemolytic disease. Bergman got the idea during a holiday in Perth...

item.description: In the English village of Botton, part of the Esk Valley Camphill Community in the North York Moors, people with and without learning disabilities live together as a community rather than as care provider and care recipient. item.title: Sardinian restaurants ban phones during family dinners
item.description: Restaurants in Sardinia are introducing a ban on phone use for families during meals. The idea is that families without screens will engage more in conversation with each other and pay more attention to one another and the meal. The story was published by The Optimist Daily, a news site focused on positive news, in the Nutrition & Wellness category.

item.title: California legalizes balcony solar panels for renters
item.description: California has legalized balcony solar energy. This means that renters and other residents can now attach solar panels to their balconies to generate their own electricity. The measure makes it possible for more people to access solar energy, even if they don't own their own roof or home. The news report provides no further details about the specific regulations, implementation...

item.description: Five years ago, 18-year-old Kenli Riney lost her life in a head-on collision on a Texas highway, her car engulfed in flames. The Argote family, passing by by chance, ran toward the fire: Mike Argote suffered severe burns while pulling Riney from the vehicle and beginning CPR, then his 14-year-old daughter Ema took over. item.description: London will host Fight Back Promotions' first boxing gala on 28 November, founded by former Team GB boxer Lesley Sackey, three-time national champion Shelly Sweeney and entrepreneur Poppy Mason-Watts. What started as a $50,000 GoFundMe campaign grew into more than $16.5 million in rental assistance.
